pr.title: Fix `ElaborateBoxDerefs` on debug varinfo
pr.description:
Slightly simplifies the `ElaborateBoxDerefs` pass to fix cases where it was applying the wrong projections to debug var infos containing places that deref boxes.

From what I can tell[^1], we don't actually have any tests (or code anywhere, really) that exercise `debug x => *(...: Box<T>)`, and it's very difficult to trigger this in surface Rust, so I wrote a custom MIR test.

What happens is that the pass was turning `*(SOME_PLACE: Box<T>)` into `*(*((((SOME_PLACE).0: Unique<T>).0: NonNull<T>).0: *const T))` in debug var infos. In particular, notice the *double deref*, which was wrong.

This is the root cause of #128554, so this PR fixes #128554 as well. The reason that async closures was affected is because of the way that we compute the [`ByMove` body](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/master/compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/coroutine/by_move_body.rs), which resulted in `*(...: Box<T>)` in debug var info. But this really has nothing to do with async closures.

[^1]: Validated by literally replacing the `if elem == PlaceElem::Deref && base_ty.is_box() { ... }` innards with a `panic!()`, which compiled all of stage2 without panicking.

analysis.summary: PR fixes `ElaborateBoxDerefs` for debug var infos whose place contains a `Deref` on `Box<T>`. The old projection-rebuilding logic duplicated the original box deref, producing an invalid double-deref place such as `*(*(((_1.0).0).0))`; the corrected pass replaces the box `Deref` with the `Unique`/`NonNull`/`*const` field projections plus exactly one `Deref`, and preserves later projections once. The focused regression test is custom MIR `debug foo => *opt;` with a MIR diff, plus a run-pass async-closure test for the downstream ICE.
analysis.originalLogic: In the old `ElaborateBoxDerefs` debug-varinfo path, the pass iterated `place.iter_projections()` with an index, kept `last_deref = 0`, and on encountering `elem == PlaceElem::Deref && base_ty.is_box()` initialized `new_projections`, appended `base.projection[last_deref..]`, appended the box field projection from `build_projection(unique_ty, nonnull_ty, ptr_ty)`, pushed a new `PlaceElem::Deref`, and set `last_deref = i`. After the loop it appended `place.projection[last_deref..]` and installed the result. For a debug place `(*_1)` where `_1: Box<i32>`, the loop base projection is empty and `last_deref` becomes `0`, so the final append re-adds the original box deref and yields two derefs.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, when elaborating a debug varinfo place that dereferences a box, the pass rewrote `Deref` on `Box<T>` into the three pointer-field projections plus a deref but then also retained/duplicated the original box `Deref`. The PR description states it turned `*(SOME_PLACE: Box<T>)` into `*(*((((SOME_PLACE).0: Unique<T>).0: NonNull<T>).0: *const T))`, and calls out the double deref as wrong. The corrected output has only one outer dereference after the field chain, e.g. `*(((_1.0).0).0)` for `debug foo => *opt`. The invalid extra deref can lead to `deref projection of non-dereferenceable ty` during validation.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies whose `VarDebugInfoContents::Place` value has a projection containing `PlaceElem::Deref` whose base type is `Box<T>`. This includes hand-written custom MIR using `debug foo => *opt;` where `opt: Box<i32>`, and compiler-generated debug var infos from by-move bodies of async closures capturing a boxed value such as `Box<dyn Trait>`. The place may also have surrounding projections before or after the box deref, not only a bare `*_1`.
analysis.trigger: A `VarDebugInfoContents::Place` contains a `Deref` projection on a base of type `Box<T>`, so `ElaborateBoxDerefs` must elaborate that box dereference in the debug-info place. The bug is specifically exercised by debug var infos, not by ordinary non-debuginfo places, and historically was not covered by existing tests or stage2 code.
preconditions: The MIR body has a debug varinfo whose value is a `Place`.
That place's projection includes `PlaceElem::Deref` with `base_ty.is_box()` true.
The box deref may be the first projection, as in `debug foo => *opt` with `opt: Box<i32>`, or may be surrounded by other projections.
For a minimal hand-written reproducer, use `#![feature(custom_mir, core_intrinsics)]`, `#[custom_mir(dialect = "built")]`, and `mir!(debug foo => *opt; { Return() })`.
For the end-to-end async-closure failure, use an async closure that captures/moves a `Box<dyn Trait>` and invokes methods through it, as in the `box-deref-in-debuginfo.rs` run-pass test.
pitfalls: Do not treat the old double deref as a legitimate alternate rewrite; the PR explicitly identifies it as wrong: `In particular, notice the *double deref*, which was wrong.`

Do not infer the bug from the test expectation alone: the decoded new-revision before-pass MIR is `debug foo => (*_1);`, and the corrected after-pass MIR is `debug foo => (*(((_1.0).0).0));` with a single deref.
The failure is in the debug-varinfo rewrite path; ordinary MIR place elaboration may already behave correctly, so tests must inspect debug varinfos.
Once elaboration starts, subsequent non-box projections must be appended exactly once; the old post-loop append caused duplication.
Do not conflate this with borrowing restrictions or post-copy overwrite issues; the reported symptom is an invalid extra deref projection and an ICE in validation.
The ICE issue is about async closures only incidentally; the root cause is `ElaborateBoxDerefs` on a debug varinfo containing a box-deref place.
The added MIR test uses `// skip-filecheck`, `//@ test-mir-pass: ElaborateBoxDerefs`, and an `EMIT_MIR` diff; without the diff it would not check the corrected projection chain.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a focused custom-MIR MIR-opt test with `#[custom_mir(dialect = "built")] fn pointee(opt: Box<i32>)` containing `debug foo => *opt;`, marked `//@ test-mir-pass: ElaborateBoxDerefs`, and emit/check the post-pass MIR diff. The corrected expectation is a single dereference after the `Unique`/`NonNull`/`*const` field chain, `debug foo => (*(((_1.0: std::ptr::Unique<i32>).0: std::ptr::NonNull<i32>).0: *const i32));`; the historically wrong output had an additional outer deref. Also include the run-pass async-closure regression (`tests/ui/async-await/async-closures/box-deref-in-debuginfo.rs`) with `block-on.rs` aux build to cover the downstream ICE path. Keep ordinary non-debuginfo box-deref tests unchanged so the two variants differ only in the debug-varinfo transformation.
evidence: Slightly simplifies the `ElaborateBoxDerefs` pass to fix cases where it was applying the wrong projections to debug var infos containing places that deref boxes.

What happens is that the pass was turning `*(SOME_PLACE: Box<T>)` into `*(*((((SOME_PLACE).0: Unique<T>).0: NonNull<T>).0: *const T))` in debug var infos. In particular, notice the *double deref*, which was wrong.
This is the root cause of #128554, so this PR fixes #128554 as well.
